title: Closed-Form Arbitrary-Gap Rényi Nonadditivity Above Any Positive Order via Direct Products of Free Groups and High-Girth Graphs
authors: Guocheng Zhen, Ranyiliu Chen, Xin Wang
abstract: We give a closed-form finite-dimensional construction of quantum channels with real algebraic entries exhibiting arbitrarily large violations of minimum-output Rényi entropy additivity uniformly above any prescribed positive Rényi order, using a different finite realization based on direct products of free groups and fixed-field high-girth graphs. More precisely, for every $p_0>0$ and $g>0$, we construct one channel and one Bell input for which the additivity gap is greater than $g$ simultaneously for all $p\in[p_0,\infty]$. With $r=\lceil2g\rceil$, the construction uses $15r$ output qubits and $O(r2^{30r}+r^2(1+p_0^{-1}))$ input qubits. Compared with the stated parameters of Shou and Gorshkov \cite{ShouGorshkov2026}, our construction uses fewer output qubits for every target gap and has a smaller asymptotic input-qubit bound as the gap grows with the positive cutoff fixed. At the von Neumann order, a separate specialization gives an explicit channel with gap greater than $1/1024$ using $37608898$ input qubits and $8$ output qubits.
summary: This theoretical paper constructs quantum channels that violate the additivity of minimum-output Rényi entropy by an arbitrarily large, controllable amount. It achieves this using a sophisticated model involving direct products of free groups and high-girth graphs. The work provides explicit, closed-form bounds and compares its resource scaling favorably against previous state-of-the-art constructions.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct quantum channels that exhibit arbitrarily large violations of minimum-output Rényi entropy additivity for all Rényi orders $p$ above a positive cutoff $p_0$.
main_result: A closed-form, finite-dimensional construction is provided that guarantees the additivity gap $\Delta_p$ exceeds any prescribed positive value $g$ simultaneously for all $p \in [p_0, \infty)$.
method: The construction utilizes a novel model based on direct products of free groups and fixed-field high-girth graphs, employing spherical penalties derived from Chebyshev polynomials to establish strong compression bounds.
model_or_system: The study concerns quantum channels $\Phi: \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C}) 	o \mathcal{D}(\mathbb{C})$ acting on finite-dimensional quantum systems. The construction is explicitly realized using permutation matrices derived from graph structures.
key_observables: Minimum-output Rényi entropy additivity gap ($\Delta_p$), Rényi entropy $H_p(ho)$, and the required input/output qubit dimensions.
important_parameters: The target gap $g>0$, the Rényi order cutoff $p_0>0$, and the resulting parameters $r = \lceil 2g ceil$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of high-girth graphs and the ability to evaluate spherical averages using finite moment formulas, providing explicit certified bounds.
figures_summary: The notes mention Figure 1 illustrating the coordinate graph $D(2, 2)$ structure, which is central to defining the algebraic representations used in the construction.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general problem of nonadditivity, develops the algebraic machinery using free groups and high-girth graphs, introduces spherical penalties to create a filter, and culminates in proving the explicit, closed-form construction and comparing its resource scaling to prior art.
why_interesting: The techniques developed—combining algebraic graph theory (free groups, high-girth graphs) with quantum information measures (Rényi entropy)—provide powerful, non-standard tools for proving fundamental limitations in quantum information theory.
